introduction: On this Sunday, the Israelites complain in the desert, and God rains down bread from heaven. In the Gospel, the crowd looks for Jesus because they had eaten their fill of bread, and he says to them: I am the bread of life; whoever comes to me will never hunger. Paul calls us to put on the new self. Let us seek the food that lasts for eternal life.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Father gives us the true bread from heaven. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may lead people beyond their material needs to Christ, the bread of life. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are hungry and those who live in poverty: that they may receive their daily bread. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who spend their lives working only for what perishes: that they may discover what truly lasts. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who complain and grumble in hard times: that they may learn to trust in God's daily care. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may put off our old way of life and put on the new self, created in God's likeness. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, you fed your people with manna in the desert and you give us the true bread from heaven. Satisfy our deepest hunger with your Son. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: The bread of life
reflection.body:
Only weeks after God has set them free from Egypt, the Israelites start to complain. They even say they wish they had died in Egypt, "when we sat by the meat pots, when we ate our fill of bread." Freedom in the desert seems harder than slavery with full stomachs. God answers their grumbling with patience: "Behold, I will rain bread from the sky for you." Each morning they find something on the ground and ask, "What is it?" Moses answers, "It is the bread which the LORD has given you to eat."

In the Gospel, the crowd that was fed by the loaves goes looking for Jesus. He is honest with them: "you seek me, not because you saw signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were filled." They want another free meal. Jesus wants to give them more: "Don't work for the food which perishes, but for the food which remains to eternal life."

They ask for a sign like the manna. Jesus answers that the true bread from heaven is not something Moses gave, but something the Father gives now: "the bread of God is that which comes down out of heaven and gives life to the world." They ask, "Lord, always give us this bread." And he says, "I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will not be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty."

We all have hungers that bread cannot satisfy: for meaning, for love, for forgiveness, for God. Jesus offers himself to feed them.

Paul tells the Ephesians what that means for daily life: they must "put on the new man, who in the likeness of God has been created in righteousness and holiness of truth." This week, notice what you hunger for most. Bring that hunger to Jesus in prayer, and receive him in Communion as the bread that truly satisfies.
